SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HANDWRITING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Handwriting helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: HANDWRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas

What this means
In this part you learn to use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Handwriting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner. (skill: use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Handwriting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs.
3. Practise this skill: use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Handwriting from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Handwriting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Handwriting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when writing a 5 lessons a) use capital letters correctly  Learners are guided to write for paragraph?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Handwriting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate spacing between sustained period individually and in words pairs.
5. Be able to: use legible and neat handwriting  Learners practice effective to communicate effectively punctuation (capitalization, commas.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
